Q6039.reason: In 1997 China, India, and most other poor countries were still under this income line, so low- and lower-middle-income countries held about three-quarters of world population; 40% is the low-income-only share.

Q6181.reason: WHO/UNICEF 2017 under-five cause data put preterm birth complications first at about 18%, ahead of pneumonia (~15–16%), diarrhea (~8%), and malaria (~5%).

Q9001.reason: World Bank $1.90/day estimates put 2019 extreme poverty at about 8.4% of world population, closer to 10% than to 5%.

Q9006.reason: GTD and Global Terrorism Index counts for 2017 are roughly 19,000–26,000 deaths, the same order of magnitude as 26,000.

Q9007.reason: UNESCO’s adult (age 15+) literacy rate was about 86% in 2015; the ~91% figure is youth literacy, which is ruled out.
